touches.text: One bus per cairn instance, not per host. Each box runs its own bus, and the buses talk to one another, so a device always talks to the bus on its own box; together they are the instance's one bus. A device runs on one box; the other boxes reach it over the buses. No box needs a full set of devices. WHY: so the instance can run several heavy tasks at once across boxes.

A remote box keeps its own database and syncs it with the home box's (6.3.7.4). Node rows are the same on every box; the sync fills the blanks a box holds open (4.3.1.5.1.1). WHY: the local copy is fast, and the sync is the backup.

The stored answers are learning, so they live in the memory model: a tree the proxy holds by the librarian's delegation, asking "what did this request answer?". An answer is found by its exact request and carries no embedding (4.3.1.6). The meter (every call, its verdict and cost) is not learning: it is metrics (17.27). The inference ticket, a file in the logs tree on the 30 day clock, is only for debugging.

metric: records a measurement of anything. WHY: a metric is a primitive; its job is to measure whatever it is, and like feedback (which a metric strictly is) it must eventually have a consumer. USERS: any probe or tool.
